R101.note: Rejects any parsed URI with a non-null host and any absolute opaque URI after checking; relative redirects still pass. Clean open-redirect fix.

R102.note: Adds an IAuthorizationService/policy check in the handler before delete, matching the existing Admin role; no other observable change.

R103.note: Switches to DirContext.search(filterExpr, filterArgs, cons), which escapes per RFC 4515; explicit new SearchControls() reproduces the prior null-default behavior.

R104.note: Regex allowlist plus path.resolve/relative confinement closes the traversal; the confinement branch has confusing double-negated logic but is not wrong, and legitimate alnum plugin names are unaffected.

R105.note: allowed_classes restricted to ShoppingCart; legitimate cart deserialization and the existing instanceof check both keep working.

R106.note: Allowlists the sort column in the controller before it reaches ${sort}; tenantId binding, default sort, and the call chain all wired correctly.

R107.note: Switches to POST + ValidateAntiForgeryToken and updates the confirmation view's link to a token-bearing POST form in the same diff.

R108.note: Adds requireRole('admin') matching the exact pattern of every sibling admin route; no other change.

R109.note: Fixed code compares message.UserId, but ChatMessage only defines AuthorUserId - this will not compile.

R110.note: Allowlist regex structurally excludes every LDAP metacharacter before the filter string is built; minor risk of rejecting unusual but valid usernames.

R111.note: snprintf with return-value checks reproduces the exact 'AUDIT user:action' output and rejects oversized input rather than truncating, matching the given signature and contract.

R112.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5) correctly neutralizes the HTML body context; nothing else changes.

R113.note: Primary replacement interface drops the sort parameter from findForTenant entirely without updating InvoiceService/InvoiceController, which still call findForTenant(tenantId, sort) - breaks the existing call chain; the enum-based alternative is sketched but never wired into a real method either.

R114.note: archive/tar replaces the shell call correctly, but a plain tar.NewReader won't auto-decompress a gzip/tgz archive the way shell 'tar -tf' does, a functional regression for compressed archives that isn't mentioned.

R115.note: Uses the already content-detected extension instead of the client-supplied one; no other observable change.

R116.note: Ping-based rewrite eliminates Process.Start entirely (matches the documented C# guidance), but the response body's format/content is completely different from the original Test-Connection text output, and that difference isn't called out.

R117.note: finfo-based MIME allowlist plus a random server-generated filename closes the vector; legitimate image uploads behave the same.

R118.note: csrf-csrf double-submit tokens are an appropriate mechanism, but no error handler is shown for validation failure, so the library's default thrown error (not JSON) replaces the contract's required '403 JSON on cross-site failure', and legitimate callers now need an undisclosed extra token-fetch step first.

R119.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES) applied to both fields; minimal, no other change.

R120.note: Allowlist of sort expressions with a safe default preserves the tenant constraint, range mapping, and the original default sort.

R121.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before the write, returning early on out-of-range index; nothing else changes.

R122.note: Keeps DOMPurify's sanitized HTML for the body context and derives a tag-stripped, quote-escaped plain-text value for the title attribute, satisfying both stated contexts.

R123.note: Comprehensive control-character/line-separator escaping; moving the value into a structured meta field changes the emitted log line's shape, but that's shown directly in the diff and doesn't impede logging.

R124.note: Content-sniffed extension allowlist with a random filename on write, and the read path is updated in lockstep to only accept that new name format; the generated name is returned to the caller as the contract requires.

R125.note: strrchr-based true-extension check plus a random filename closes the double-extension bypass; no other observable change.

R126.note: Escapes control characters/line separators in place while keeping the original log template string unchanged - closes the injection with no other observable change.

R127.note: resize() fixes the reported OOB write into packet, but the stated contract also requires rejecting/reporting a count larger than the source fields vector - that check is never added, so fields[i] can still read out of bounds when count exceeds fields.size(), left unaddressed and undisclosed.

R128.note: Replaces ECB with AES-GCM and a fresh nonce prepended to the ciphertext; the format change is an unavoidable, disclosed consequence of moving off ECB, not an incidental one.

R129.note: SecureRandom replaces the attacker-seedable Random entirely; dropping the seed parameter is the point of the fix and is stated plainly.

R130.note: Removes the self-invocation by calling the repository directly and adds @PreAuthorize to the actual batch entry point, closing the AOP-proxy bypass.

R131.note: Callback-based setTimeout removes code generation entirely; recordReminder still gets called with the same values and the response shape is unchanged.

R132.note: Minimal, correct: flips setSecure(true) only; nothing else changes.

R133.note: res.sendFile with the root option is the Express-native confinement mechanism; behavior for legitimate filenames under reportsDir is unchanged.

R134.note: slog attribute escaping correctly closes the log injection, but the accompanying rewrite of main() also swaps log.Fatal for slog.Error on a ListenAndServe failure, silently dropping the process-exit-on-startup-failure behavior - not mentioned anywhere in the write-up.

R135.note: firebase/jwt's decode enforces signature verification before claims are trusted; the returned id/role shape matches the original.

R136.note: session_regenerate_id() called immediately after verification and before marking the session authenticated - standard fixation fix, nothing else changes.

R137.note: execFile with an argument array removes the shell entirely; same response behavior for legitimate domains.

R138.note: allowed_classes=>false is the correct minimal fix for the unserialize() call itself, but the stated contract requires loadCart to also return contents for a row already migrated to JSON - unserialize() on a JSON string returns false, violating the array return type and losing/crashing on migrated carts, which isn't addressed or disclosed.

R139.note: require_http_methods(['POST']) combined with the already-enabled CsrfViewMiddleware correctly closes the GET-based CSRF deletion; the docstring notes the template must switch to a POST form with a CSRF token.

R140.note: Resource-based ownership check is the right mechanism, but it returns Forbid() (403) for an unauthorized invoiceId, while the stated contract requires unauthorized IDs not reveal more than the original not-found path - this leaks invoice existence, and the write-up explicitly argues for the 403 choice instead of matching the contract.
